correctness.rationale: The finite-degree filtration identity \(N(t^i)=ia t^{i+d}+\cdots\) gives distinct independent leading pivots for all \(N^j\) while \(m\le p+d\). At \(m=p+d+1\), Frobenius forces \(N(t^p)=0\) and kills the whole ideal \(t^p A_m\); surviving lower monomials yield \(\operatorname{rank}N^j=\max(p-1-(j-1)d,0)\) at every positive \(j\). Rank profiles determine nilpotent Jordan partitions, and comparing N^2 for depth d and d+1 proves the iff collision threshold d>=p-1. A direct finite-field substitution matrix test checked 3,487 profiles and ten cross-depth comparisons; enumeration corroborates but does not prove the parameter-uniform identities.

value.rationale: The induced polynomial-module action is the canonical faithful modular representation of each finite Nottingham quotient. Its entire Jordan profile is a structural invariant more informative than fixed-point dimension; the theorem gives coefficient-independent rigidity, the optimal truncation threshold where it fails, and an iff collision criterion separating group ramification depth from linear similarity. The first-wild boundary is a natural characteristic threshold, not an arbitrary finite slice, and its short-range similarity census is complete.
